verdict.summary: Gate 1 (your own workspace) and Gate 2 (unlisted public distribution) are self-serve. Gate 3 (Marketplace listing) is a human review that Slack says it cannot shorten, requires at least 10 active workspace installs first, and runs for weeks. Composio's default scope list also includes scopes that trigger enhanced review, so you should trim it before any Marketplace submission.
verdict.hands_on_effort: Gate 1-2: about 1-3 hours. Gate 3: several days of preparation (privacy policy, support page, landing page, test workspace, install counts) plus feedback rounds.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 30 minutes after you create the app, if you connect your own account through Composio using your own app.
verdict.approval_wait: Gate 2: none reported (community source only, verify). Gate 3: up to 10 weeks for the functional review of new submissions per one Slack page; Slack pages give conflicting timelines (see open questions).

gates.name: Own-workspace install (no provider term found in findings)
gates.unlocks: Create the Slack app and install it in its own development workspace. Connect your own account through Composio using your own app.
limits: By default, a newly built Slack app can only be installed in its associated workspace.
Composio managed OAuth (no own app) is enough for internal or testing use.

gates.name: Unlisted public distribution (Manage Distribution > Activate Public Distribution)
gates.unlocks: Other workspaces can install the app through an install link. The app is not in the Slack Marketplace. Slack's docs position this for pilots with early customers.
limits: Community sources say no Slack review is needed to activate distribution. Verify this on the current Manage Distribution page before relying on it.

Unlisted commercially distributed apps created after May 29, 2025 have conversations.history and conversations.replies limited to 1 request per minute and 15 objects per request, unless approved for the Marketplace.
Existing unlisted installs were moved to the same limits from March 3, 2026.
Some workspaces allow installation only by admins, or only apps listed in the Slack Marketplace.
OAuth tokens do not expire unless revoked. Token rotation is opt-in for granular-permission apps.
gates.time_to_reach: Under an hour once the checklist is complete. Community sources say it takes effect immediately.

gates.name: Slack Marketplace listing (review)
gates.unlocks: Public listing in the Slack Marketplace, and removal of the unlisted rate limits on conversations.history and conversations.replies.
limits: Requires at least 10 installations on active workspaces (active = used in the past 28 days), and that count must hold through the whole review.
Slack says it cannot shorten or skip the review and may require multiple feedback rounds.
All feedback must be addressed before listing.
Apps using scopes that trigger enhanced review get a longer review.
gates.time_to_reach: Up to 10 weeks for the functional review of new submissions per one Slack page; other Slack pages give different figures. Plus time to reach 10 active-workspace installs.

steps.title: Create the Slack app
steps.detail: Sign in to api.slack.com/apps with the Slack account that owns the development workspace. Create a new app in your development workspace. Slack apps (not classic apps) are the supported model.
gotchas: Classic apps are deprecating. Slack pushed the classic-app deprecation date to November 16, 2026, so do not build on a classic app.
The exact create-app menu label was not verified. Follow the current on-screen flow.

steps.title: Set the Redirect URI
steps.detail: Open App Management > OAuth & Permissions and add the redirect URL. Redirect URLs must use HTTPS. The value must match the redirect_uri used in both the authorize step and the token exchange step.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: A mismatched redirect_uri returns bad_redirect_uri at the token exchange.

Composio's default redirect is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add. Use this only if you stay on Composio's own app. If you use your own app, register the callback URL shown in your Composio auth config.

steps.title: Trim the bot and user scope list
steps.detail: Under OAuth & Permissions, add only the scopes your agent needs. Do not copy Composio's full default list. Its default list includes scopes that trigger enhanced Marketplace review, including search:read.*, *:history, files:read, groups:write and mpim:write.

values.label: Scope list
values.value: Only scopes your agent uses. Review each enhanced-review scope before adding it.

gotchas: Scopes that give extensive workspace data access without a clear use case are listed as unsuitable for the Marketplace.
User-token scopes should be used only when the app acts as the authenticating user.

steps.title: Draft scope justifications and an app manifest
steps.detail: Given the final scope list and the agent's use cases, draft a one-line justification per scope and a short description of what each scope is used for. Mark which scopes are needed for core features and which are optional. The developer reviews the draft before it is used.
gotchas: Reviewers expect a justification for each scope. Mark scopes as optional only if the app works without them.

steps.title: Decide on optional scopes and token rotation
steps.detail: Mark any non-essential scopes as optional so users can install without granting them. Decide whether to enable token rotation. Rotation is opt-in for granular-permission apps and gives you a refresh token plus an expiring access token. Without it, tokens do not expire unless revoked.
gotchas: Rotation prerequisites beyond granular permissions and the expiry length of rotated tokens were not confirmed. Check the current docs before enabling it.

steps.title: Connect your own account through Composio using your app
steps.detail: Install the app in your development workspace from the install link on the OAuth & Permissions or Install App page. Then add your app's Client ID and Client Secret to a Composio auth config for the slack toolkit and authorize your own account. Confirm the agent can call one scope-limited API method.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The exact Composio field names for entering client credentials were not verified here.
Authorization codes expire after ten minutes. Complete the exchange promptly if you test manually.

steps.title: Activate public distribution (Gate 2)
steps.detail: Open Manage Distribution. Under Share Your App with Other Workspaces, complete every item in the checklist. Then click Activate Public Distribution. This produces an embeddable Add to Slack button and an install link.

values.label: Menu
values.value: Manage Distribution > Share Your App with Other Workspaces > Activate Public Distribution

gotchas: The full checklist was not read. Only that items must be completed first is confirmed.
Community sources say no review is needed. Verify on the current page before you tell customers they can install.

steps.title: Test an install in a second workspace
steps.detail: Install the app in a workspace that is not your development workspace using the install link. Check install, onboarding and uninstall. Some workspaces block installs by non-admins, or allow only Marketplace-listed apps.
gotchas: Some workspaces allow only apps listed in the Slack Marketplace. Those customers cannot install an unlisted app.

steps.title: Plan around the unlisted rate limits
steps.detail: Check which methods the agent calls. If it uses conversations.history or conversations.replies in an unlisted commercial app, model the limit of 1 request per minute and 15 objects per request. Design for caching, narrower queries or fewer calls. The developer reviews the plan.
gotchas: This limit applies to unlisted commercially distributed apps created after May 29, 2025, and to existing unlisted installs from March 3, 2026.
Slack's API terms say the Marketplace is the only appropriate channel for commercially distributing Slack-API apps. Plan commercial rollout with that in mind.

steps.title: Prepare Marketplace requirements (Gate 3)
steps.detail: Publish a privacy policy with a clear link, a publicly accessible landing page that does not sit behind login, and a publicly accessible support page. Build the app so it is fully functional and installable, and uninstall works.
gotchas: The review team tests install, onboarding and uninstall on a workspace that is not your development workspace.
Slack's guidelines require a clear privacy policy link. Have the page live before submission.

steps.title: Reach 10 active-workspace installs
steps.detail: Get the app installed on at least 10 workspaces that were used in the past 28 days. Keep that count stable through the whole review. Slack also looks at weekly active users (fewer than 10 is not ready to list).
steps.est_time: Weeks to months, depending on your pipeline
gotchas: Blocked from submitting if below 10 active workspaces.
Active workspace means used in the past 28 days.

steps.title: Submit for Marketplace review
steps.detail: Submit from the app's Marketplace or Manage Distribution page once the prerequisites are met. Include the scope justifications drafted earlier. Note that enhanced-review scopes make the review longer.
gotchas: Do not submit before the 10-install prerequisite holds.

steps.title: Wait for review and address feedback
steps.detail: Slack reviews the submission in stages and may require multiple feedback rounds. Respond to every point before listing. Slack will not shorten or skip the review.
steps.est_time: Up to 10 weeks per one Slack page (other timelines conflict)
gotchas: Review timelines are stated inconsistently across Slack pages. Plan for the longest figure.
Resubmitting changes for published apps can take about 6 weeks per the same page.

requirements.item: Slack developer app with Redirect URL set to the Composio callback (HTTPS)
requirements.detail: Redirect URL must use HTTPS and match in authorize and token exchange.
A new app installs only in its associated workspace by default.
Complete the Share Your App with Other Workspaces checklist, then Activate Public Distribution.

requirements.item: Accept unlisted rate limits on conversations.history and conversations.replies
requirements.detail: 1 request per minute and 15 objects per request for unlisted commercial apps created after May 29, 2025.
A clear link to your privacy policy is required for Marketplace review.

requirements.item: Publicly accessible landing page and support page
requirements.detail: The landing page must not sit behind login. A public support page is required.

requirements.item: At least 10 installations on active workspaces
requirements.detail: Active means used in the past 28 days. Count must hold through the review.

requirements.item: Fully functional, installable and uninstallable app
requirements.detail: Review team tests on a non-development workspace.
Reviewers expect a justification for each scope. Enhanced-review scopes lengthen review.

scopes.scope: search:read.* (search:read, search:read.files, search:read.im, search:read.mpim, search:read.private, search:read.public, search:read.users)
scopes.effect: Triggers enhanced Marketplace review. Remove unless the agent needs search.
Triggers enhanced Marketplace review. Also falls under the unlisted rate limits for conversations.history when used for that method.
Triggers enhanced Marketplace review. Remove unless the agent needs to modify private channels or group DMs.
Triggers enhanced Marketplace review. Do not add unless there is a clear use case.
Use only when the app acts as the authenticating user. Reviewers check this.
Can mark individual scopes optional so users can install without granting them all.

blockers.symptom: conversations.history or conversations.replies calls are throttled to 1 request per minute and 15 objects per request.
blockers.cause: Unlisted commercially distributed apps created after May 29, 2025, and existing unlisted installs from March 3, 2026, get the lower limits unless the app is approved for the Marketplace.
blockers.fix: Plan for the limit (caching, narrower queries) or pursue Marketplace approval, which requires the 10-install prerequisite and review.

blockers.symptom: Slack will not accept a Marketplace submission, or the app is blocked from submitting.
blockers.cause: Apps need at least 10 installations on active workspaces (used in the past 28 days) before submission.
blockers.fix: Build installs to at least 10 active workspaces before submitting, and keep the count stable through review.

blockers.symptom: Slack review rejects or requests changes related to scopes or data access.
blockers.cause: Legacy or restricted scopes, or scopes that give extensive workspace data access without a clear use case, are unsuitable for the Marketplace. Composio's default scope list includes several enhanced-review scopes.
blockers.fix: Trim the scope list to what the agent needs, justify each scope, and drop search:read.*, *:history, files:read, groups:write and mpim:write unless required.

blockers.symptom: Some customer workspaces cannot install the app.
blockers.cause: Some workspaces restrict installs to admins, or allow only apps listed in the Slack Marketplace.
blockers.fix: Tell customers that admin approval may be needed. For workspaces that allow only Marketplace apps, Marketplace listing is the only path.

blockers.symptom: Commercial rollout through an unlisted app is questioned by Slack.
blockers.cause: Slack's API terms say the Slack Marketplace is the only appropriate channel for commercially distributing Slack-API apps, whether unlisted or custom one-off apps.
blockers.fix: Confirm your distribution model with Slack before commercial rollout. Plan to submit to the Marketplace for commercial distribution at scale.

blockers.symptom: Redirect fails at the token exchange with bad_redirect_uri.
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri in the token request does not match the one in the original authorize request or the app's configured Redirect URL.
blockers.fix: Use the exact Composio callback URL in the app's Redirect URL and in the Composio auth config.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed Slack OAuth app for internal or testing use. You need your own Slack app to distribute to other workspaces (Manage Distribution), to control your own redirect URL and scope list, or to pursue a Marketplace listing. Composio's default scope list includes several scopes that Slack's Marketplace guidelines flag for enhanced review (search:read.*, groups:write, mpim:write, *:history, files:read), so trim the list for your own app.

open_questions: Developer-portal prerequisites (free Slack account, Developer Program signup, paid plan, org admin, business verification) were not confirmed from an official Slack page.
The exact app-creation menu label and the full Manage Distribution checklist were not read. Only that checklist items must be completed before Activate Public Distribution is confirmed.
Whether Activate Public Distribution needs no Slack review is supported only by community sources. Verify on the current Manage Distribution page.
Marketplace review timelines conflict across Slack pages: 10 business days / 10 weeks; 1 week / 7 weeks; 1 week / 8 weeks; 2-3 weeks / 6-8 weeks. The most recent authoritative page was not confirmed.

No official install cap for unreviewed or unlisted apps was found. The listing prerequisite of 10 active workspaces is not an install cap. Test-user limits and dev-mode restrictions were not documented in the sources read.
Whether Composio's managed Slack app is subject to Slack's enhanced review or distribution limits was not verified.
Probing the authorize endpoint with an invalid client_id returned HTTP 200 with no OAuth error. Behavior for unknown clients is not confirmed.
Token rotation prerequisites beyond granular permissions and the expiry length of rotated access tokens were not confirmed.
Marketplace common rejection reasons beyond scope/data and privacy/support were not read from the official review guide.
Exact Composio field names for entering the client ID and secret into a slack auth config were not verified.
